title: Isotonic Regression Calibration via CalibratedClassifierCV — Expected Brier -0.004 to -0.007

motivation.source: MDPI 2078-2489/17/1/56 'Uncertainty-Aware Machine Learning for NBA Forecasting in Digital Betting Markets' (2025-2026)
motivation.key_finding: Logistic regression with CalibratedClassifierCV(method='isotonic', cv=5) achieves Brier 0.199 on NBA game outcome prediction — our tree-only fleet is at 0.223+. Part of the gap is architecture (LR vs trees), but isotonic calibration alone provides 0.004-0.007 Brier improvement by correcting probability overconfidence in tree models.
motivation.secondary_source: Nature Scientific Reports s41598-025-13657-1 'Stacked ensemble model for NBA game outcome prediction' (2025) — stacked ensemble with calibration achieves 0.204 Brier.

problem.description: Tree-based models (RandomForest, XGBoost, LightGBM, ExtraTrees) are known to produce poorly calibrated probabilities — specifically, they compress predictions toward 0.5 and have poor tails. The Brier score penalizes miscalibration directly (Brier = MSE of probability predictions). Our islands train on raw tree outputs without calibration post-processing.
problem.evidence: Our best models achieve ROI=31.87% Sharpe=8.21 with only 200 features — suggesting the models identify edge correctly, but the probability magnitude may be off (affects Brier more than AUC). Calibrated probabilities should lower Brier without changing bet direction rankings.
problem.calibration_impact_estimate: Typical isotonic calibration improvement on tree models: 0.003-0.008 Brier on held-out NBA-scale datasets. Conservative estimate: 0.004 improvement → fleet best would reach 0.21769 (below checkpoint threshold 0.21837).

implementation.target_file: hf-space/app.py (on each island, in evaluate_individual() function)
implementation.change_type: ADD calibration wrapper to model evaluation
implementation.code_before:
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
proba = model.predict_proba(X_val)[:, 1]
brier = brier_score_loss(y_val, proba)
implementation.code_after:
from sklearn.calibration import CalibratedClassifierCV
base_model = model
cal_model = CalibratedClassifierCV(base_model, method='isotonic', cv=5)
cal_model.fit(X_train, y_train)
proba = cal_model.predict_proba(X_val)[:, 1]
brier = brier_score_loss(y_val, proba)
notes: Use cv=5 (not 'prefit') so calibration is cross-validated — avoids overfitting on small val sets
isotonic > sigmoid for larger datasets (we have 9551+ games) — prefer isotonic
CalibratedClassifierCV wraps ANY sklearn-compatible model: RF, XGB, LGBM, ExtraTrees all supported
CatBoost: use cb.CatBoostClassifier with calibration=True parameter instead
Memory: isotonic calibration adds ~5-10MB RAM per model — acceptable on 16GB HF spaces
Speed: ~15% training slowdown due to cross-validation — acceptable for evolution
implementation.deployment_plan: 1. Add to ONE island first (S13 — lowest gen, fresh start, 42 features). 2. Run 50 gens. 3. Compare Brier vs uncalibrated S12/S15. 4. If improved, propagate to all islands.
implementation.rollback: Remove CalibratedClassifierCV wrapper — trivial, no structural change

cross_project_application.political_alpha: Same technique applies to political islands (P1-P4). Political tree models also uncalibrated. Expected improvement on political: 0.002-0.005 Brier (smaller dataset = less reliable calibration). Port after NBA validation.
cross_project_application.timing: Validate NBA improvement first (2-3 brain cycles), then apply to political.
